games.title: Adventureland
games.note: Written in BASIC for a 16 KB TRS-80; often called the first text adventure sold for a home computer.

games.title: Mystery House
games.note: Often called the first adventure game with graphics; Roberta Williams based its plot on Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None.

games.title: Wizard and the Princess
games.note: On-Line Systems' second Hi-Res Adventure and one of the first adventure games drawn in colour.

games.title: Softporn Adventure
games.note: A comic text adventure published by On-Line Systems, later Sierra; Al Lowe remade it as Leisure Suit Larry.

games.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
games.note: Douglas Adams co-designed it with Infocom's Steve Meretzky, loosely following his novel.

games.title: King's Quest
games.note: Commissioned by IBM for the PCjr; you walk an animated hero around the screen while typing commands.

games.title: Space Quest: The Sarien Encounter
games.note: Made by the 'Two Guys from Andromeda', starring the hapless space janitor Roger Wilco.

games.title: Police Quest: In Pursuit of the Death Angel
games.note: Designed by former California Highway Patrol officer Jim Walls around real police procedure.

games.title: Leisure Suit Larry in the Land of the Lounge Lizards
games.note: Opened with a quiz of trivia questions meant to keep children out.

games.title: Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Fathers
games.note: Jane Jensen's voodoo murder mystery set in New Orleans; Tim Curry voiced Gabriel in the CD version.

games.title: Phantasmagoria
games.note: A full-motion-video horror game with live actors that shipped on seven CDs.

games.title: Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders
games.note: A tabloid reporter battles aliens who plan to make humanity stupid through the phone network.

games.title: Loom
games.note: Spells are four-note melodies played on a distaff, and there is no inventory at all.

games.title: Sam & Max Hit the Road
games.note: Based on Steve Purcell's comics about a canine detective and a hyperkinetic rabbity thing.

games.title: Full Throttle
games.note: Tim Schafer's first game as project leader, about a biker gang leader framed for murder.

games.title: The Dig
games.note: Based on an idea by Steven Spielberg; it spent about six years in development.

games.title: Grim Fandango
games.note: A film noir set in the Land of the Dead, mixing Day of the Dead imagery with art deco.

games.title: The Curse of Monkey Island
games.note: The first Monkey Island without Ron Gilbert, and the last LucasArts game built on the SCUMM engine.

games.title: Thimbleweed Park
games.note: Funded on Kickstarter in 2014 by the two creators of Maniac Mansion.

games.title: Return to Monkey Island
games.note: Ron Gilbert's first Monkey Island since 1991, picking up where Monkey Island 2 ended.

games.title: Simon the Sorcerer
games.note: Written by Simon Woodroffe and produced by his father Mike; Red Dwarf's Chris Barrie voiced Simon in the CD version.

games.title: Simon the Sorcerer II: The Lion, the Wizard and the Wardrobe
games.note: The sequel's subtitle spoofs C. S. Lewis; Chris Barrie returned as the voice of Simon.

games.title: Lure of the Temptress
games.note: Revolution's first game introduced its Virtual Theatre engine, where characters go about their own routines.

games.title: Beneath a Steel Sky
games.note: A cyberpunk adventure drawn with Watchmen artist Dave Gibbons, released as freeware in 2003.

games.title: Broken Sword: The Shadow of the Templars
games.note: Released as Circle of Blood in North America; it opens with a café bombing in Paris.

games.title: Discworld
games.note: Based on Terry Pratchett's novels, with Eric Idle voicing the inept wizard Rincewind.

games.title: The Longest Journey
games.note: Art student April Ryan travels between Stark, a world of science, and Arcadia, a world of magic.

games.title: Dreamfall: The Longest Journey
games.note: Moved the series into 3D with a new heroine, Zoë Castillo, alongside April Ryan.

games.title: The Manhole
games.note: A HyperCard storybook for children with no goal, just places to explore by clicking.

games.title: Myst
games.note: Built in HyperCard by two brothers; it was the best-selling PC game until The Sims overtook it in 2002.

games.title: Riven
games.note: The sequel to Myst shipped on five CDs after about four years of work.

games.title: Obduction
games.note: Funded on Kickstarter in 2013 as Cyan's spiritual successor to Myst and Riven.

games.title: The Witness
games.note: Jonathan Blow spent about seven years and much of his Braid earnings making it.

games.title: Braid
games.note: A puzzle platformer built on rewinding time, and one of the first big indie hits on Xbox Live Arcade.

games.title: Blue Prince
games.note: Each day you draft a new floor plan of a 45-room manor; Ros dedicated the game to Maze author Christopher Manson.

games.title: Little Big Adventure
games.note: Released as Relentless: Twinsen's Adventure in North America.

links.took: A text adventure of rooms, treasures and two-word commands.
links.added: Squeezed the format into 16 KB on a TRS-80 and sold it, starting a commercial genre.

src.t: Scott Adams's account, Wikipedia: Adventureland (video game)

links.extra: Adams played Crowther and Woods's Adventure on a mainframe at work before writing his own.

links.took: The text adventure itself: exploring rooms and solving puzzles by typing commands.
links.added: Drew every room as a picture on the Apple II and turned it into a murder mystery.

src.t: Roberta and Ken Williams, interview, Time Extension, 2023

links.extra: Roberta Williams said she had never played a computer game before Adventure; it led to On-Line Systems, later Sierra.

links.took: Colossal Cave popularized the typed two-word text adventure this game is built on.
links.added: Turned the format into a bawdy comedy about chasing romance in a seedy city.

links.took: Colossal Cave popularized the parser adventure: typed commands, treasures and puzzles.
links.added: An animated hero you walk around a storybook kingdom seen from the side.

links.took: Infocom's text parser and Z-machine engine, first built for Zork.
links.added: Douglas Adams's comedy, a sarcastic narrator and famously unfair puzzles.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (video game)

links.took: A non-linear world you explore at your own pace, solving puzzles to make progress.
links.added: Replaced typed text with rendered pictures you click through, with almost no instructions.

src.t: Robyn Miller, GDC 2013 postmortem, reported by MTV
Medium, 'Two histories of Myst', on Rand Miller

links.extra: Both Miller brothers had played Zork; otherwise they played few video games.

links.took: Designer Brian Moriarty came from Infocom, where he wrote Wishbringer, Trinity and Beyond Zork.
links.added: A short fairy tale told through musical spells, with no inventory and no typing.

links.took: The same husband-and-wife team and the same picture-plus-parser format.
links.added: A fantasy quest drawn in colour instead of black-and-white line art.

links.took: Roberta Williams's fairy-tale fantasy adventures for her own company.
links.added: Animated characters walking through the scenes instead of still pictures.

links.took: Roberta Williams's picture-based adventure design, four years on.
links.added: An animated hero you steer around the screen, built for IBM's PCjr.

links.took: Roberta Williams returning to murder and dread in a creepy old house.
links.added: Live actors on video, gore and a seven-CD horror story.

links.took: Sierra's AGI engine, built for King's Quest: an animated hero plus typed commands.
links.added: Science-fiction comedy starring a janitor, with sudden and often silly deaths.

src.t: Wikipedia: Space Quest: The Sarien Encounter

links.took: Sierra's AGI engine and animated adventure format from King's Quest.
links.added: Realistic police procedure: skip a safety check and the game punishes you.

src.t: Wikipedia: Police Quest: In Pursuit of the Death Angel

links.took: Sierra's AGI engine and parser-driven animated adventures.
links.added: Adult comedy about a hapless man on the town, with an age-check quiz.

src.t: Wikipedia: Leisure Suit Larry in the Land of the Lounge Lizards

links.took: Its plot and puzzles: Al Lowe remade Softporn Adventure at Ken Williams's request.
links.added: Graphics, the character Larry Laffer and Al Lowe's self-mocking humour.

src.t: Wikipedia: Leisure Suit Larry in the Land of the Lounge Lizards

links.extra: Sierra had published Softporn Adventure, a 1981 text game, as On-Line Systems.

links.took: Seeing a young cousin play King's Quest gave Ron Gilbert the push to make a graphic adventure.
links.added: Clickable verbs instead of typing, a team of three kids chosen from seven, several endings.
links.extra: Gilbert hated guessing words for King's Quest's text parser, so Maniac Mansion put the verbs on screen.

links.took: Jane Jensen learned adventure design at Sierra, co-designing King's Quest VI with Roberta Williams.
links.added: A dark, adult mystery about voodoo murders, deeply researched in New Orleans history.

links.took: Roberta Williams's Sierra adventure design from the King's Quest series.
links.added: Swapped storybook fantasy for horror, with live actors filmed against blue screen.

links.took: The SCUMM engine and verb interface built for Maniac Mansion.
links.added: A globe-trotting plot with four playable characters split across continents.

src.t: Wikipedia: Zak McKracken and the Alien Mindbenders

links.took: Lucasfilm's SCUMM engine, first built for Maniac Mansion.
links.added: Dropped the verbs entirely: you play musical notes to cast spells.

links.took: Ron Gilbert's SCUMM engine and verbs; he co-designed it with David Fox and Noah Falstein.
links.added: Followed the film's story, with fistfights and 'Indy Quotient' points for alternate solutions.

src.t: Wikipedia: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade: The Graphic Adventure

links.took: Ron Gilbert's SCUMM engine and on-screen verbs.
links.added: A pirate comedy designed to avoid deaths and dead ends, plus insult swordfighting.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Secret of Monkey Island

links.took: Ron Gilbert and Gary Winnick reunited to make a new game in Maniac Mansion's style.
links.added: Five playable characters, a murder mystery and an X-Files-style small town.

links.took: Tim Schafer and Dave Grossman co-wrote Monkey Island, then co-led Day of the Tentacle.
links.added: Time-travel puzzles across three eras and Chuck Jones-style cartoon animation.

links.took: LucasArts' SCUMM engine and cartoon slapstick, released five months after Day of the Tentacle.
links.added: Replaced the verb list with a cursor you cycle through, plus a road trip across America.

src.t: Wikipedia: Sam & Max Hit the Road

links.took: Tim Schafer co-led Day of the Tentacle before leading his own project.
links.added: A gritty biker story with a pop-up icon menu, action scenes and full voice acting.

links.took: Loom designer Brian Moriarty led The Dig for a time before Sean Clark finished it.
links.added: A serious science-fiction story about astronauts stranded on an alien world.

links.took: Tim Schafer's cinematic, character-driven adventure writing.
links.added: 3D characters, a noir story spanning four years and the Land of the Dead.

links.took: Alone in the Dark popularized 3D characters on pre-rendered backgrounds with fixed camera angles.
links.added: Used that look for a noir comedy, steered with tank-style keyboard controls.

links.took: Tim Schafer left LucasArts after Grim Fandango and founded Double Fine.
links.added: Moved from adventure games to a 3D platformer set inside characters' minds.

links.took: Built on Grim Fandango's GrimE engine, with 3D characters on pre-rendered backgrounds.
links.added: Brought Monkey Island into 3D, with keyboard controls and Monkey Kombat.

links.took: Guybrush, Elaine and LeChuck, picking up after Monkey Island 2's strange ending.
links.added: Lush hand-drawn cartoon art, full voice acting and a point-and-click verb coin.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Curse of Monkey Island

links.took: The Monkey Island cast, setting and comedy from Curse.
links.added: A move to 3D and keyboard control.

links.took: Picks up right after Monkey Island 2's ending, with Guybrush, LeChuck and Elaine.
links.added: A new hand-drawn look, a built-in hint book and an ending about memory.

links.took: Terrible Toybox, the studio Ron Gilbert ran for Thimbleweed Park.
links.added: Returned to Monkey Island with Dave Grossman, working with Lucasfilm Games.

links.took: Comic fantasy and an on-screen verb bar; the Woodroffes called Monkey Island an obvious inspiration.
links.added: A sarcastic British teenage wizard and parodies of fairy tales and Tolkien.

src.t: Simon Woodroffe, via Wikipedia: Simon the Sorcerer

links.extra: Woodroffe also cited Terry Pratchett's Discworld books, Red Dwarf, Fawlty Towers and Monty Python, and aimed for British humour.

links.took: Adventure Soft began as Adventure International UK, porting Scott Adams's text adventures.
links.added: Mike Woodroffe's company grew from text-game ports into animated point-and-click comedy.

src.t: Mike Woodroffe, interview, The Adventure Gamer, 2016

links.took: Simon, his fairy-tale world and the verb-bar interface.
links.added: A bigger world and more parodies as the evil wizard Sordid returns.

links.took: Revolution's Virtual Theatre engine, where characters follow their own routines.
links.added: A dystopian cyberpunk city drawn with comics artist Dave Gibbons.

links.took: Revolution's Virtual Theatre engine and Charles Cecil's story-driven design.
links.added: Hand-drawn cartoon animation and a globe-trotting Templar conspiracy.

src.t: Wikipedia: Broken Sword: The Shadow of the Templars

links.took: Monkey Island popularized the comic point-and-click adventure that Discworld follows.
links.added: Terry Pratchett's world and jokes, with Eric Idle as the bumbling Rincewind.

links.took: A dark, story-heavy adventure; Ragnar Tørnquist named it among his chief inspirations.
links.added: Two parallel worlds, one of science and one of magic, and a long coming-of-age story.

src.t: Review quoting Tørnquist, Only Solitaire, The Longest Journey

links.extra: Tørnquist also cited Neil Gaiman's Sandman and Buffy the Vampire Slayer.

links.took: The twin worlds of Stark and Arcadia, and April Ryan.
links.added: 3D exploration, stealth and fight scenes, and a new lead, Zoë Castillo.

links.took: Cyan's click-to-explore HyperCard worlds, made by the Miller brothers for children.
links.added: A mysterious island for adults, with rendered 3D scenes and hard puzzles.

links.took: Myst's first-person click-through exploration and the story of Atrus's family.
links.added: One large, coherent world whose puzzles depend on understanding its culture.

links.took: Cyan's first-person puzzle exploration, made as a spiritual successor to Myst.
links.added: Real-time 3D in Unreal Engine 4, VR support and swapping pieces of alien worlds.

links.took: Cyan's dense, culture-driven world design from Riven.
links.added: Crowdfunding and a new universe of seeds that trade places between worlds.

links.took: A deserted island of mysterious structures to explore at your own pace.
links.added: Hundreds of line-drawing panels that teach their own rules without any words.

src.t: Jonathan Blow and Rand Miller, Dev on Dev, PlayStation Blog, 2017

links.extra: Blow told Rand Miller that Myst and Riven were both huge influences, and called the game a deliberate homage.

links.took: Puzzles woven into the environment, solved by noticing how the world works.
links.added: Hidden environmental puzzles you can only see from the right spot.

src.t: Jonathan Blow and Rand Miller, Dev on Dev, PlayStation Blog, 2017

links.took: Jonathan Blow's puzzle design, which teaches through play rather than text.
links.added: Moved from a 2D platformer to an open 3D island of line puzzles.

links.took: A quiet, mysterious place full of interlocking puzzles, from Tonda Ros's long fascination with Myst.
links.added: A manor you redraft each day by choosing rooms like cards in a board game.

links.took: Deep, layered puzzles hidden in the world, named with Myst in Ros's origin story.
links.added: Daily runs that reset the house while your knowledge carries over.
links.extra: Ros's main inspiration was Christopher Manson's 1985 puzzle book Maze; drafting board games also shaped it.

links.took: Frédérick Raynal left Infogrames after Alone in the Dark to found Adeline Software.
links.added: A colourful isometric world and switchable moods: normal, sporty, aggressive or discreet.
